facts: Upstream officially documents Linux/macOS/Windows, not Android.
The frozen binding.gyp uses the Unix target on non-Windows and links -lutil.
Official Node v22.19.0 android_configure.py supplies OS=android and android_ndk_path, so the common Termux missing-android_ndk_path failure is not assumed to apply to this carrier.
Koffi does not list Android in its official support matrix.
The frozen 3.1.6 is newer than the 3.1.5 release that removed the statx libc-wrapper build problem.
Android/Termux source-build success is useful evidence but is not accepted as APK/NDK carrier evidence.
The frozen lock contains sharp@0.35.4 and exact @img/sharp-wasm32@0.35.4 with sha512 integrity.
The frozen lock also contains @emnapi/runtime@1.11.3 required by sharp-wasm32.
Lock presence does not prove host-specific npm ci materialized optional WASM bytes; the manual G2 device probe checks this explicitly.
Android carrier image processing remains NOT_RUN until a real sharp create→PNG buffer smoke passes.

fallback.loaderBehavior: sharp 0.35.4 falls through to @img/sharp-wasm32/sharp.node when no native runtimePlatform case loads.

facts: @vscode/ripgrep@1.18.0 constructs @vscode/ripgrep-${process.platform}-${arch}; Android therefore asks for an unpublished Android package.
Official alpha.4 tool-fs-search resolveRgPath() accepts no parameter and has no rgPath/ripgrepPath config or environment seam; Node mode directly imports @vscode/ripgrep.
The only official executable sidecar path is gated by 'pkg' in process; the Android Node carrier is not a pkg single-file runtime.
Official alpha.4 search-core.ts was audited at Git blob 60ea042d4f31f0e9c856536b8b34e2687482eec7.
Community will not copy/fork the official glob/grep implementation solely to replace binary resolution; doing so would create a second tool authority.
A future unlock requires either a real upstream Android @vscode/ripgrep platform package or an explicit official tool-fs-search executable-path seam.
forbiddenShortcuts: copy/fork official glob/grep implementation solely to replace binary resolution

facts: Android replaces only the shipped subprocess provider row in place with AndroidSubprocessRuntime, a subclass of official LocalSubprocessRuntime; ordinary resolve/spawn/tree/collect/spill behavior remains upstream-owned.
Only spawnTerminal() is Android-specific and uses exact node-pty@1.2.0-beta.15 plus AndroidProcessInspector.
The inspector reads only /proc/<pid>/stat PID/starttime, PPID, PGRP, session, foreground group and state; PID+starttime fences reuse and no /proc/<pid>/mem or syscall state is read.
inputWaiting=false is intentional and compatible with the official terminal-bash prompt/foreground and inferred-idle fallbacks; the official terminalInspector test hook is not used.
spawnTerminal() enforces the official MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS grace contract and starts from scrubbedParentEnv() with explicit undefined tombstones.

The embedded app-UID preflight is wired before official DSH spawn and now requires node-pty allocation, PTY root/session/PGRP/tpgid/tty facts, foreground-group signal-0 visibility, output delivery, and a node-pty exit event.
Wiring is not evidence. Frozen node-pty Android build/load, the app-UID preflight, and a real shipped minimal persistent-terminal session remain required before terminal evidence can leave BLOCKED.
The official ctx.sandbox abstract provider seam is public and stable in @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox.

Android composition replaces the shipped sandbox row in place by id with the Community provider through the official --patch layer; the ctx.sandbox service id and row order are preserved and no official bundle is modified.
The Community provider uses official writableRoots(policy), preserves exit-125 plus landlock-run signature classification, and advertises full only after an exact fully-enforced launcher probe.
The frozen runtime lock contains @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run@0.1.1, whose npm payload publishes src/main.c; the Android NDK probe builds that source unmodified.

The embedded Node bootstrap is wired to run android-app-uid-preflight.cjs before official DSH spawn; it repeats the full probe and proves an allowed write plus a denied sibling write under the APK app UID.
The preflight wiring is not evidence. Sandbox remains blocked until a real APK run records PASS.
alpha.4 session materialization uses link()+unlink() on every non-win32 platform.
alpha.4 attachment publication also uses link() before removing the staging name.
The embedded Node bootstrap now performs an actual fs.linkSync() inode/link-count/content probe inside the Android app data directory before official DSH starts.
Only execution under the APK app UID can promote evidence; source presence and Linux CI execution cannot.

conclusion: Android Local remains blocked. First-party sandbox and subprocess providers are wired through official seams; hard-link, Landlock, and PTY substrate checks are fail-closed before official DSH spawn. Real Node/NDK/native-addon and APK app-UID evidence, a shipped minimal persistent-terminal user path, sharp device execution, and the upstream-blocked fs-search seam remain open.

subprocess.reason: AndroidSubprocessRuntime is wired in place through the official provider seam and subclasses official LocalSubprocessRuntime. Remaining proof is frozen node-pty Android build/load, the real APK app-UID PTY preflight, and a shipped minimal persistent-terminal user path; source wiring is not evidence.
